BUTTERWORTH_Q.doc: The Q of a second-order Butterworth section, 1/√2 — maximally flat, the one value every Butterworth biquad in the tree designs at: the LR4 crossover section, the pitch pre-filter and the drive's tilt / band / HF sections, in TS and (as `OMX_BUTTERWORTH_Q`) in C (§7, the scalar door).

ALLPASS_LIMITS.doc: The first-order all-pass section's contract tolerance. `unityTolerance` is the fraction of the larger side within which the block energy identity (the sum of y squared plus the pole times the end state squared equals the sum of x squared plus the pole times the start state squared) must hold, which is what makes the section unity magnitude. A design constant of the primitive, not a control: no row serves it.

XOVER_LIMITS.doc: The Linkwitz-Riley crossover primitives' numbers. `lr2SectionQ` is the Q of the one cookbook section an LR2 crossover runs per band (a squared first-order Butterworth, critically damped); `lr4SectionQ` is the Q of each of the two sections an LR4 crossover runs (a squared second-order Butterworth); `partitionTolerance` is the fraction of max(1, block peak) within which the low and high outputs must sum to the all-pass output. Measured worst case 9e-8. Design constants and tolerances, not controls.

FDELAY_MOD_READ_ORDER.doc: The order the chorus and flanger construct their lines with (four taps).

FDELAY_READ_L1_NORM.doc: `Λ` for the chorus/flanger read — ONE value; the header and every law read this.

GATE_CONTINUOUS_TRAVELS.doc: The gate's threshold, range, release and ratio as a plugin host draws them: GATE_LIMITS' bounds, units and defaults with no step. The console's row quantises these four to whole steps (1 dB, 10 ms, 1:1), and a travel whose step is 1 or more reads as an integer control; the omx-strip plugin has always offered them continuous, so it reads this table instead. Every number but the step is GATE_LIMITS', held equal by test/continuous-travels.test.mjs. Not rendered to C: no C reader needs a second spelling of the gate's bounds.

COMP_CONTINUOUS_TRAVELS.doc: The compressor's threshold and release as a plugin host draws them: COMP_LIMITS' bounds, units and defaults with no step. The console's row quantises them to whole steps (1 dB, 10 ms), and a travel whose step is 1 or more reads as an integer control; the omx-strip plugin has always offered them continuous, so it reads this table instead. Every number but the step is COMP_LIMITS', held equal by test/continuous-travels.test.mjs. Not rendered to C: no C reader needs a second spelling of the compressor's bounds.

PARAM_SCALES.doc: How a host draws a parameter: linear, logarithmic (a frequency, a time) or in discrete steps. The words omx-plugins' declarations and plugin-hostd's protocol use; a travel names its own with `scale`.

EQ_CONTINUOUS_TRAVELS.doc: The EQ's three frequency travels as a host draws them: the band frequency, the high-pass corner and the low-pass corner, EQ_FREQ_RANGE's, HPF_FREQ_RANGE's and LPF_FREQ_RANGE's bounds with no step and a logarithmic scale. The console's EQ quantises frequency to 10 Hz; a frequency drags continuously on a log axis, which is how every host draws it, so this is the form the omx-plugins read. Every number but the step is the source's, held equal by test/continuous-travels.test.mjs. Not rendered to C: no C reader needs a second spelling of the EQ's bounds.

READOUT_RATE_HZ.doc: How often a readout's value is published: 50 Hz, one value every 20 ms, the rate a host sends a moving meter at. Every readout reads it as its `rateHz` (docs/readouts.md).

BIQUAD_KINDS.doc: The biquad section kinds the EQ design builds, in the order of the integer a kernel reads: the bell, the two shelves, the pass filters, the notch, the bandpass (the de-esser's detector band, never an EQ band), and the first- and second-order allpasses (the dynamic EQ's and the phase tool's sections). The design itself is omx-dsp's `omx_eq_design`; the console draws its curves from a twin of it, and both dispatch on this list. No come-up id: a kind is chosen by the stage that designs the section.
